title: Qubit Pharmaceuticals, Sorbonne Université, and Q-CTRL Demonstrate 3D Protein Hydration-Site Prediction on IBM Heron Processors - Quantum Computing Report
gist: Qubit Pharmaceuticals, Sorbonne Universite (CNRS LCT) and Q-CTRL ran 3D protein-pocket hydration-site prediction as a QUBO on 156-qubit IBM Heron processors (up to 123 qubits used), finding exact optimal water placements on all 11 instances and, at 123 qubits, a better solution in 25 minutes than CPLEX reached before a 3-hour timeout; they project practical drug-discovery utility at ~900 qubits and ~100,000 two-qubit gates.

insights.claim: Qubit Pharmaceuticals, Sorbonne Universite and Q-CTRL demonstrated 3D protein-pocket hydration-site prediction on 156-qubit IBM Heron processors, running hardware experiments up to 123 qubits across five FDA-approved drug-target protein structures with Q-CTRL's Fire Opal solver (published in Physical Review Research).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A peer-reviewed pharma use case on IBM hardware supports IBM's and Q-CTRL's commercial narrative in drug discovery.
insights.locator: Researchers from Qubit Pharmaceuticals, Sorbonne Université

insights.claim: Across 11 protein-ligand instances of 41-116 qubits on IBM Kingston (Heron r2), Q-CTRL's error-suppressed variational solver recovered the exact CPLEX-verified optimal water configuration in every case, with ~9% sampling probability for the optimum at 116 qubits versus ~2% for classical simulated annealing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A ~4.5x higher hit rate than simulated annealing is evidence that error-suppression software extracts real optimization value from noisy hardware.

insights.claim: On a 123-qubit hard QUBO (PDB 3b7e with ligand) on IBM Pittsburgh (Heron r3), the quantum solver found a lower-cost solution (C=-321.32) in 25 minutes of QPU time than CPLEX reached before timing out at 3 hours (C=-319.90, 40% optimality gap).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A head-to-head win against a leading exact classical solver on a real problem instance is the kind of utility signal that moves enterprise quantum adoption, though at a single instance.
insights.quote: yielded a lower-energy solution in 25 minutes of QPU runtime than the exact classical solver CPLEX achieved before hitting a three-hour timeout
insights.locator: Scaling the 3b7e protein-ligand complex to 123 qubits

insights.claim: The team fitted continuous 3D-RISM water densities to a Gaussian Mixture Model cast as a Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) problem, turning hydration-site placement into a combinatorial optimization solvable on quantum hardware.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Reformulating a chemistry problem as QUBO is a reusable template for bringing drug-discovery workloads onto near-term quantum optimizers.
insights.locator: By fitting continuous 3D Reference Interaction Site Model

insights.claim: In classical scale-up from 900 to 6,824 binary variables via simulated annealing, crystal-water recovery rose from ~60% at 123 variables to ~90% at 1,450 or more variables, matching Hydraprot precision and outperforming Placevent, Watgen and Dowser++.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Method accuracy depends on problem size far beyond current quantum-hardware scale, implying quantum advantage here requires much larger devices.

insights.claim: Extrapolating from 156-qubit Heron compilations, the authors project that hydration-site prediction becomes competitive with leading classical tools at roughly 900 qubits and 100,000 two-qubit gates, reducible to ~15,000 two-qubit gates with higher qubit connectivity.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defines a concrete hardware milestone for pharma quantum utility; higher-connectivity architectures cut gate counts ~6-7x, a point in their favor.
insights.locator: To chart the path toward practical computer-aided drug discovery

insights.claim: The authors argue full-pocket water placement for molecular docking and lead optimization is within reach of early error-corrected quantum processors.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Positions drug discovery as an early fault-tolerant application, relevant for pharma partners such as Qubit Pharmaceuticals.
